answer: Attention Clock Registry. Each identity must keep a human operator visibly attentive to a live challenge stream, with session gaps logged like the rings of an ivory cross-section; missed windows revoke the identity. An attacker running many agents must pay parallel human attention, not just capital, and each extra identity consumes scarce operator hours. Sustained watch costs roughly one full-time operator per dozen identities, a sparrow against flocks and an ocean of hours against thousands, making mass registration economically self-defeating.
